about.body1: Tap any term — get a context-aware translation that knows the book's domain. Tap «attention» in an ML chapter and you get «увага (механізм у нейромережах)» in Ukrainian, not the everyday meaning. Words you save feed a capped weekly SRS queue with multiple-choice cards generated by a local Gemma 4 model running on a $20 VPS — no per-user cloud costs.
about.creator.bio1: I built TextStack because I quit Designing Data-Intensive Applications three times before this. Not because the book was hard — I understood most of what was on the page — but because forty unfamiliar terms broke my flow. Summarizing it away defeated the point. So I built the thing I wanted: tap a term, get the context, keep reading.
about.creator.bio2: It's an open project I run because I needed it. AGPL-3.0, full codebase on GitHub. If you share the use case or want to contribute, I'd love to hear from you.
about.creator.heading: The Creator
about.intro: TextStack is an open-source reader for developers who want to finish dense English technical books in their native language.
about.mission1: Real understanding of a technical book comes from finishing it — not from skipping unfamiliar terms or summarizing it away. TextStack is built around that: keep the book in front of you, let the friction (vocabulary, terminology, domain) get out of the way.
about.mission2: Every feature — domain-aware translation, vocabulary builder, spaced repetition, reading stats — exists for one job: get you to the last page of the kind of book you usually quit halfway through.
about.openSource1: TextStack is licensed under GNU AGPL-3.0. The full codebase — .NET 10 backend, React frontend, React Native mobile app — lives at github.com/mrviduus/textstack. You can self-host the entire stack on a $20/month consumer VPS, no GPU required.
about.seoDesc: Open-source reader for developers who want to finish dense English technical books in their native language. Local LLM, AGPL-3.0, self-hostable on a $20 VPS.
about.seoTitle: About TextStack — open-source reader for developers
about.tech1: Local Gemma 4 model (via Ollama) generates the multiple-choice distractors, vocabulary hints, and book metadata enrichment on your own server — no per-user cloud LLM costs. OpenAI's gpt-4.1-nano handles the translation layer where multilingual quality matters.
about.techStackValue: ASP.NET Core 10 · PostgreSQL 16 · React 19 · React Native (Expo) · Ollama (Gemma 4) · OpenAI gpt-4.1-nano · Docker · Cloudflare Tunnel

privacy.aiBody1: Most are optional: if you do not use the tutor, Explain or translation, those features send nothing. Uploading a book is the exception — it always sends the title, author and the opening of the first chapter to OpenAI, as described above.
privacy.aiBody2: AI output can be wrong. Explanations, translations and answers about a book are generated by a language model and should not be relied on as fact.
privacy.aiBody3: We do not train models on your content, and under OpenAI's API terms neither do they. We do keep records of AI requests, as described above, for quality and cost monitoring.
privacy.aiBody4: If an AI response is offensive or harmful, please report it using the contact address at the bottom of this page.
privacy.changesBody: If this policy changes materially we will update the date at the top, and for significant changes we will say so in the app or on the site. The October 2026 revision adds what earlier versions left out: the guest account the mobile app creates, what an upload sends to OpenAI and Open Library, mobile crash reporting, app updates, backups and log retention.
privacy.childrenBody: TextStack is not directed to children under 13 and we do not knowingly collect their personal information. If you believe a child has created an account, contact us and we will remove it.
privacy.collectBody1: Account. Your email address, display name, and a profile picture if you set one. If you sign in with Google or Apple we receive your email, name, profile image URL and a provider identifier. If you use a password, we store a cryptographic hash of it and never the password itself. A guest account has only a random identifier and a made-up placeholder address.
privacy.collectBody2: Content you create or upload. The books you upload — both the original file and the text extracted from it — plus your highlights, notes, bookmarks, saved vocabulary and collections. Uploaded books are private to your account.
privacy.collectBody3: Reading activity. Reading sessions (duration, words read, position), progress, goals, streaks and achievements. This is stored on our servers and linked to your account — guest or registered — which is what lets it sync across your devices. We use it to run the app, not for analytics.
privacy.collectBody4: AI interaction data. We keep records of AI requests: every tutor and upload-enrichment request, and a sample of translation and Explain requests. A record holds the text that was sent — the passage of the book, your question — and the model's answer. These request records are not linked to your account; email addresses and phone numbers are removed from them, but the passage and question are kept as sent. The tutor is the exception: its sessions, and the record of how it planned them, are saved with your account. We use these records to investigate quality problems and to monitor what the service costs to run.
privacy.collectBody5: Technical data. IP address, server request logs, rate-limiting counters, and device and operating-system type. Our web server's request logs record the IP address and the address of each page or API call, but not the part after the "?" — so the text you send to be read aloud and the words you search for are not written to them. On the website only, analytics events if you accept analytics cookies.
privacy.collectBody6: Kept only on your device. Theme, fonts, reader layout preferences, and the offline copies of any books you download.
privacy.collectBody7: From the mobile app. If the app crashes or an error occurs, a crash report goes to Sentry: the error, the app version, the device model and operating system, a random installation identifier and a sample of performance timings. It carries no name or email, and the text of your requests is removed from it. When the app checks for updates it sends Expo a random installation identifier, the app version and the platform.
privacy.contactBody: Questions about this policy, or a request about your data? Reach out at
privacy.cookiesBody1: Essential storage keeps you signed in and remembers your reader preferences. It cannot be switched off without breaking the service.
privacy.cookiesBody2: The website asks for your consent before loading Google Analytics and Ahrefs Analytics. Analytics stays off until you accept, and you can decline. We use no advertising cookies, and the mobile apps ship no analytics or advertising SDKs at all.
privacy.intro: This policy explains what TextStack collects, why, who we send it to, and how long we keep it. It covers the textstack.app website and the TextStack mobile apps.
privacy.purposeBody: To run the reading service and sync your library across devices; to produce AI answers, explanations, translations, speech and book details when you ask for them or upload a book; to fix crashes; to prevent abuse and enforce rate limits; and to monitor reliability and what the service costs to operate.
privacy.retentionBody1: Account data and the content you create are kept until you delete them, or until you delete your account. A guest account that has been inactive for 30 days and holds nothing you saved — no books, library, progress, highlights, notes, bookmarks or vocabulary — is deleted automatically. A guest account that holds saved data is kept until you delete it or register.
privacy.retentionBody2: Cached translations, explanations and generated speech are deleted after 30 days. Our web server's request logs (which leave out the part of an address after the "?") are deleted after 14 days. Application logs are capped by size and overwritten as new entries arrive, typically within days to a few weeks. Crash and error reports are kept for Sentry's retention period.
privacy.retentionBody3: AI request records are kept indefinitely — they are the operational record of what the service did and what it cost. They are not linked to your account, but they can contain the text that was sent. Tutor records saved with your account lose that link, or are deleted, when you delete the account.
privacy.retentionBody4: Backups. We back up the database and stored files every night: two recent copies on our server and encrypted off-site copies at Cloudflare, kept for up to about three months. Data you delete stays in those backups until they expire.
privacy.rightsBody1: You can access and export your data, correct it, or delete it. Deleting your account takes effect immediately and cannot be undone: the account, uploaded books, highlights, notes, vocabulary, reading history and stored files are removed in a single transaction. Copies in backups, caches, logs and crash reports expire on the schedule above.
privacy.rightsBody2: In the app: open the Profile tab, scroll to Delete account (or Delete guest data, for a guest account), and confirm. On the website: sign in, open the user menu, choose Edit profile, then use the Danger zone. You can also start a deletion request without signing in from the page below.
privacy.rightsHeading: Your rights, and how to use them
privacy.scopeBody1: TextStack is a reading platform. This policy covers the textstack.app website and the TextStack apps for Android and iOS.
privacy.scopeBody2: You can browse the public library without an account. On the website, reading without an account keeps your progress on your device until you upload a book or save a few words. In the mobile app, opening a book or the upload screen creates a guest account on our servers straight away, so your progress, highlights and vocabulary are stored there from the start, without a name or email.
privacy.scopeHeading: Who we are and what this covers
privacy.securityBody: Data travels over HTTPS and is stored on servers we control. Books you upload are private to your account. Backups are encrypted before they leave our server. Access to production systems is limited to the operator.
privacy.seoDesc: What TextStack collects, who receives it, and how long we keep it — including the AI features.
privacy.thirdPartiesAnalytics: Google Analytics and Ahrefs Analytics. On the textstack.app website only, and only after you accept analytics cookies. The mobile apps contain no analytics.
privacy.thirdPartiesAuth: Google and Apple. Only if you choose to sign in with them, and only to verify who you are.
privacy.thirdPartiesCloudflare: Cloudflare. Carries all traffic to the service as our DNS and network provider, and stores our encrypted off-site backups.
privacy.thirdPartiesEmail: Resend. Receives your email address in order to deliver transactional email such as a password reset.
privacy.thirdPartiesIntro: We do not sell your personal information and we do not share it with advertisers or data brokers. We do send data to the providers below, each only as far as a feature you used requires.
privacy.thirdPartiesOllama: Some AI work stays with us. The hints and multiple-choice options in vocabulary review are generated by a model running on our own servers and are not sent to anyone.
privacy.thirdPartiesConnectors: Assistants you connect yourself. If you connect TextStack to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or another assistant, that assistant can read the books, highlights, notes and vocabulary you give it access to, and write notes and words back. You start this connection and can revoke it; what the assistant does with the data is covered by its own privacy policy.
privacy.thirdPartiesOpenai: OpenAI. Receives book text in four cases: when you use translation (model gpt-4.1-nano), Explain or the tutor (gpt-4.1-mini) — your question and the relevant passage — and, automatically, every time you upload a book: its title, author and the opening of its first chapter (a few hundred characters) are sent to fill in missing details such as genre, year and description. Under OpenAI's API terms this content is not used to train their models.
privacy.thirdPartiesSentry: Sentry. Receives error and performance data from our servers and from the mobile app when something fails, as described above. Server reports can include details of the failing request. Sentry keeps them for its own retention period.
privacy.thirdPartiesExpo: Expo. Delivers updates to the mobile app; receives an installation identifier, the app version and the platform each time the app checks for one.
privacy.thirdPartiesTts: Microsoft. Text you ask to be read aloud — a passage, a word, a saved sentence — is sent to Microsoft's Edge text-to-speech service to be turned into audio. We use the same public service the Edge browser uses for reading aloud; we have no separate agreement with Microsoft.
privacy.thirdPartiesOpenLibrary: Open Library (Internet Archive). When you upload a book, we look up its title and author in Open Library's public catalogue to fill in missing details. Only the title and author are sent.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.transfersBody: Several of the providers above — OpenAI, Microsoft, Open Library, Google, Apple, Resend, Sentry, Expo and Cloudflare — process data in the United States and elsewhere. Using the features that depend on them transfers your data there.
